text:
Sean Gallagher: Heads up: we need to lock capacity windows for latency/$ benchmark runs (multi-region) so we don’t clobber prod. Can we align on:
1) windows per region (NA/EU/APAC)
2) monitoring + guardrails
3) escalation path + go/no-go criteria

Vanessa Ortiz: Yep. I pulled rough availability from Fleet. Proposed windows (local time):
- us-east (IAD): Tue 02:00–05:00 ET
- us-west (SJC): Tue 02:00–05:00 PT
- eu-west (DUB): Wed 01:00–04:00 GMT
- ap-northeast (TYO): Thu 01:00–04:00 JST
These are “low traffic” but not zero. We need safety limits.

Neha Kapoor: +1. Requirement: benchmark MUST run behind guardrails (no shared pools w/ top-tier prod routes unless we cap hard). Also want explicit rollback: if p95 latency increases > X% on shared infra, we stop.

Rina Kobayashi: For benchmark-lab we can set concurrency caps + request rate shaping. We can also force to benchmark-only route group if you give me the region headers / routing tags.

Mina Haddad: Routing-wise we can pin to `bench=true` tier in each region. Caveat: eu-west is currently sharing some GPU nodes w/ normal Hosted traffic during off-peak. If we want hard isolation we need Dedicated-style slice or strict caps.

Sean Gallagher: Let’s assume partial sharing in eu-west and ap-northeast unless Fleet can isolate. Vanessa, can we reserve “bench slice” (even if smaller) in those regions?

Vanessa Ortiz: We can reserve 8x H100 in eu-west and 4x H100 in ap-northeast as a temporary slice. us-east/us-west we can do 8x each. That should cover the planned matrix if the harness doesn’t exceed ~70% GPU util.

Keiko Yamamoto: Harness can set `--max-gpu-util=0.70` and `--max-inflight-reqs` per model. Also we can disable autoscale burst for the bench slice so it doesn’t steal capacity.

Claire Dubois: For methodology, we need consistent settings across regions. Please don’t vary batching/caching flags region-by-region unless it’s purely safety-related and we document it.

Jonas Weber: Agree. If we must cap harder in one region, we call it out in the appendix + rerun with same cap elsewhere for comparability.

Peter Holtz: On guardrails: can we define the stop conditions concretely?
- If any shared pool shows p95 > +10% vs baseline for 10 min -> stop
- If error rate > 1% sustained for 5 min -> stop
- If GPU mem OOMs start appearing -> stop

Owen Phillips: Add “tail spikes” detection too. Sometimes averages look fine but p99 blows up when KV cache thrashes. Suggest we track:
- p50/p95/p99 latency on critical prod routes
- queue depth / batch queue time
- KV cache hit rate + evictions (if exposed)

Logan Wright: We can wire a dedicated dashboard view w/ side-by-side: bench slice vs prod slice.
I can also set up a quick log-based alert on `bench=true` to catch runaway retries.

Sean Gallagher: Monitoring requirements (proposal):
Dashboards (per region):
- Region health: overall req/s, errors, p95/p99, saturation
- GPU: util, mem, SM occupancy, throttling
- Runtime: queue depth, batch size dist, prefill vs decode time
- Routing: % traffic on bench tier, fallback events

Alerts during window (temporary):
- Prod p95 regression >10% (10m)
- Prod error rate >0.5% above baseline (5m)
- Bench slice GPU util >75% (5m)
- Bench slice OOM count >= 1 (immediate)

Does anyone object to thresholds?

Neha Kapoor: Tighten prod error trigger to +0.25% above baseline for the duration. Launch week we cannot explain a spike with “benchmarking.”

Rina Kobayashi: Works. I’ll keep harness concurrency modest initially and step up after warmup. Plan:
- 15 min warmup (discard)
- 30 min run #1
- 10 min cool down
- 30 min run #2
(Repeat only if variance gate fails)

Claire Dubois: Please ensure warmup doesn’t populate shared caches if we’re measuring “steady state.” Our internal policy is: warmup allowed but report explicitly that results include warmed runtime.

Jonas Weber: +1. Also: we should record “capacity window metadata” (region, slice size, any throttles) for audit.

Vanessa Ortiz: I’ll create a single doc w/ reservation IDs + exact node pools. (link) https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Benchmark+Capacity+Windows+Plan

Peter Holtz: Escalation path during runs:
- Primary: #eng-sre + @Sean Gallagher (run commander)
- On-call SRE: pager via PagerDuty if any prod alerts trigger
- Runtime on-call: @Owen Phillips (or whoever is on that week)
- Fleet/capacity: @Vanessa Ortiz
- Routing: @Mina Haddad
Stop-the-line authority: SRE RC (Sean) + SRE on-call.

Sean Gallagher: Yep. Also want a dedicated war-room channel during windows? Maybe `#bench-warroom` for the 4 nights.

Neha Kapoor: Do it. Also require explicit go/no-go at T-15 min:
- confirm no existing incidents
- confirm prod p95 within normal band
- confirm slice allocated in region
- confirm alerts armed

Grafana: (automation) Created dashboard folder: “Benchmark Windows”
- us-east overview: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/bench-us-east
- us-west overview: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/bench-us-west
- eu-west overview: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/bench-eu-west
- ap-northeast overview: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/bench-ap-northeast

Logan Wright: Added temp alert rules (disabled by default). Need someone to enable at start of each window.

Rina Kobayashi: Operational question: do we want to block bench traffic from triggering autoscaling in shared pools? We had a case where rate-limited traffic still moved HPA.

Keiko Yamamoto: For bench slice we can pin replicas and disable HPA scale-up. For shared: can set `bench=true` to a separate deployment that doesn’t influence prod HPA metrics.

Mina Haddad: Confirmed: route policy can send bench to separate service in each region. I’ll add a hard denylist to prevent accidental routing to prod service.

PagerDuty: Acknowledged: Temporary routing incident policy created for “Benchmark Window” (expires in 7 days).

Sean Gallagher: Great. Action items:
- Vanessa: finalize slice reservations + post reservation IDs in the Confluence page
- Logan: ensure dashboards + alerts are ready, plus quick “how to enable/disable” snippet
- Mina/Keiko: ensure bench tier is isolated and cannot spill into prod
- Rina: share exact run schedule + expected peak concurrency per region
- Neha: approve final thresholds + stop conditions

We’ll do a 10-min dry run in us-east on Monday 01:30 ET to validate alerting + routing. :thumbsup:
